newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-NEW MARSEILLE SIDE BEGINS TO TAKE SHAPE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NEW MARSEILLE SIDE BEGINS TO TAKE SHAPE.

text.p: Marseille, in the middle of a rebuilding programme aimed at putting the club back among Europe's elite, are expected to sign two new players next week -- with more to follow soon.
"Claude Makelele and Anto Drobnjak will sign next week," the club's sporting director and former player Marcel Dib said on Tuesday.
Drobnjak, a Yugoslav international striker currently with Bastia, could sign even earlier. Bastia play Marseille in a friendly on Friday.
Makelele, a versatile attacking midfielder, is set to sign from Nantes, while defender Serge Blanc of Montpellier has all but signed.
Marseille, whose first season back in the top flight has been a disappointment, are also close to enticing Auxerre captain Franck Silvestre and Rennes defender Patrice Carteron south.
It has also been rumoured that Bordeaux coach Rolland Courbis will take over from Gerard Gili as coach, although no official announcement has been made about that.
Marseille are also said to be looking for one big foreign name, which could be a libero as young Italian Ivan Franceschini is returning to Parma.
They are retaining German goalkeeper Andreas Koepke but Bulgaria midfielder Yordan Lechkov's future at the club is uncertain.
